content: New data shows public bodies paid private consultants £3.4bn last year, with government spending rising £1.3bn since 2019-20 and staying well above pre-pandemic levels. The figures highlight a major issue for Keir Starmer’s government, which wants to cut consultant spending by half during this parliament. Since Labour took office, almost £650m in new consulting contracts have been awarded, including a KPMG deal worth up to £223m to train civil servants. Labour peer Prem Sikka condemned the heavy reliance on consultants, arguing they add limited value and cannot quickly grasp complex organisations well enough to produce useful reports.
